activities.caption: bet before you read on — which offence tops lived experience
activities.name: crimFraudPredict

config.q: Picture 'crime'. Now: which offence does the national victimisation survey find people experience most often?
choices: Fraud — deceiving people and organisations out of money or property
config.why: Millions of incidents a year — yet the public picture is burglary or violence. The picture is manufactured by reporting, recording and media selection.

activities.anchor: AC1.1 names a set of crime types, and the unit requires you to analyse each along the same four axes
activities.caption: pair each type with its awareness signature
activities.name: crimAxesMatch

config.prompt: Pair each type with its awareness signature:

pairs.right: diffuse victims, a respectable logo — loses the coverage contest, awareness stays low
the offender writes the rules — awareness depends on journalists, whistleblowers, international bodies
borderless and fast-moving, often undetected by the person harmed until long after
survey estimates run to hundreds of thousands while recorded counts sit in the low thousands

config.why: Offence, victims, offenders, awareness — the last one ties everything together.

activities.anchor: Each reason predicts a different remedy
activities.caption: why crime goes unreported — file each reason
activities.name: crimUnreportedSort

items.label: fear of the offender, or of not being believed
a scam that looks like bad luck — no knowledge a crime occurred
complexity: 'who do I even tell about a frozen crypto account?'
culture-bound offences where reporting would betray the community itself
'it was only a phone' — feeling not really affected

config.why: Fear responds to support and anonymity; ignorance to campaigns; complexity to specialised channels — which is how Action Fraud and True Vision came to exist.

activities.anchor: and confusing the two is the standard error this unit exists to prevent
activities.caption: how awareness of domestic abuse was re-manufactured
activities.name: crimDAOrder

config.prompt: The domestic-abuse case, step by step — put it in order:
items: The dark figure is exposed by surveys and campaigns in the 1970s–90s
The recorded numbers go up — with no necessary change on the street
config.why: A rising statistic can mean rising crime or rising confidence to report — the subtlety the whole unit turns on.

activities.anchor: the 1960s Mods and Rockers were his case
activities.caption: the media machinery, part by part
activities.name: crimMediaMatch

config.prompt: The media machinery — pair each part with its effect:

pairs.right: a group cast as the symbol of society's fears — concern spikes, punishments escalate beyond what the trend justifies
immediacy, dramatisation, personalisation — distortion independent of any editor's intention
heavy followers estimate rates higher than the statistics and feel more fearful
shortens the panic cycle to days; unverified clips stand in for statistics

config.why: Violent and sexual offences over-shown, common offences under-shown — coverage measures what makes a story, not what makes a statistic.

activities.anchor: so if the media are full of stabbings, stabbings must be rising
activities.caption: the street vs the bulletins — drag the divider
activities.name: crimNewsCompare

config.prompt: The street vs the bulletins — drag the divider:

before.label: the street
before.text: common offences dominate by volume — most never dramatic, most never shown

after.label: the bulletins
after.text: selection favours the dramatic, the visual, the personal: violent and sexual offences over-shown, the most common offences under-shown

config.why: Coverage measures what makes a story, not what makes a statistic — a moral panic can run with no underlying trend at all.

activities.anchor: The 60 that never got past the victim are invisible to every table built from police data.
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the two instruments
activities.name: crimInstrumentsSpot

config.prompt: One of these instrument claims is wrong — click it:
lines: Recorded figures are an administrative count of what the system processes.
Murder is essentially complete in the recorded count — there are no unreported murders for long.
The survey is immune to recording-rule changes and captures the dark figure.
The survey's main household sample includes businesses and children under 16.
Read them together, or not at all.
config.correction: The household survey misses businesses and children under 16 in the main sample — each instrument has its own blind spots.
config.why: Triangulate: neither is the true rate; each has its own reliability, validity and ethics.

activities.anchor: reliably reports a higher crime rate than the police count
activities.caption: call the reach of the US self-report study
activities.name: crimNCVSEst

config.prompt: The US National Crime Victimization Survey — how many people does it study each year?
config.why: Around 160,000 respondents a year — and, like any questionnaire, it misses some populations and depends on victim recall.
config.context: Paired with the FBI's Uniform Crime Reports from around 17,000 agencies — the same two-instrument logic worldwide.
